items.title: What we've been playing - "Shoving Moon Flesh into an alien grandma's mouth"
items.summary: Our regular article where we tell you what we've been playing so you'll tell us what you've been playing. Deal?
items.content:
A few of the things that have us hooked this week.

Image credit: Digital Extremes Feature by Matt Wales Associate Editor Published on Oct. 24, 2026, 7 a.m. 117 comments Follow Nintendo Switch Sports Resort Prioritise us on Google 24th October Hello, it is me, your regular weekend host Mertie and I am here once again to guide you gently into Saturday with our usual feature What We've Been Playing, where we write a little about the games we've been, yes, playing. This week, Bertie - before fleeing for a well-deserved break and leaving me with the keys to the place - runs a one-on-one D&D game; Connor plays with his Moon Flesh in Warframe , and I've been serenely gallivanting over yonder hills.

But enough about us, what about you? What have you been playing this week? Do tell all! And don't forget we have an entire archive of previous What We've Been Playings for your leisurely perusal, just in case you forgot what you were playing a year or a month or a week ago.

I'm a little busy outside of work at the moment with rehearsals for a play I'm in (The Importance of Being Ernest), but I did find time for another Dungeons & Dragons first: a one-on-one game. I've been wanting to do one of these for a while, and, as I discovered recently, one-on-one games are a whole thing. Duets, they're called, rather poetically. You need to modify campaigns a bit to be playable this way, because most are designed for groups of four or five people, and you probably need to give a player a companion character as backup. But otherwise, it's totally doable. Some people make adventures exclusively for one-on-one games .

I ran a mini-adventure called D8 Night , created by the now-closed dice shop Dakota Irish. It's a nice, warm two-hour-or-so affair, where the player is caught in a time-stilled village and tasked by some magical mischief maker to retrieve the components of a romantic meal before being allowed to leave. It's a simple enough set-up, and as with a lot of things D&D, the set-up doesn't really matter so much as the playing of it and the unexpected things that happen. And unexpected things did happen. I played with my partner so I know her likes pretty well, I like to think - that's the attraction of a one-on-one set-up like this - but I didn't expect her to connect so strongly with some of the incidental characters. This resulted in entire areas being imagined-to-life that weren't written on paper. The imagination never ceases to amaze me.

Anyway, I'm off to Comic Con this weekend to celebrate my birthday - it'll be my birthday when you're reading this. I'm off to geek-out about Critical Role and watch the new Laika animated film, and to stuff my face with food.

I had a lovely time playing developer Funselektor's Art of Rally follow-up Over the Hill last week, roaming its beautifully stylised wilderness expanses in my cheerful 4x4 so I could write some words about it all . But it clearly got its hooks into me, and I went on to spend pretty much my entire Saturday just pootling around the Canadian Valhallas, the Algerian desert, thoroughly transfixed by the tranquil rhythms of it all.

It really is a game for the curious - and the infinitely patient. As the old meme goes: See that mountain?, you can climb it. Just be prepared for a lot of slow-going, a lot of trial-and-error, and a lot of determination. But while it should be frustrating, the opposite somehow ends up being true, and it's easy to feel at peace in this striking wilderness, guitars strumming gentle encouragement as you become one with the world.

You haven't experienced FOMO until you've experienced MMO do-this-or-you'll-never-be-able-to-do-it-again FOMO: The once-in-a-lifetime grinds, the cosmetics that may be vaguely impressive to onlookers in a decade's time, and the first-thing-in-the-morning, last-thing-at-night routines of logging on and doing busywork.

For those unaware, Warframe is currently bracing for a journey into a whole new galaxy. The trip requires fuel, but given we're talking about the big-red-number-loving, fashion-forward, weirdly wonderful Warframe here, this fuel isn't diesel. No, Warframe players in their thousands are currently shoving Moon Flesh into an alien grandma's mouth.

We're taking parts of Eris - a grim petri dish home to countless infested ghouls - and, fouler still, the Mesa warframe. Like a ripe cheese, its stink is what meemaw craves, and providing it brings great rewards. These include weapons and dead-handy consumables like Legendary Cores and Archon Shards, but perhaps more delectable are the cosmetics. Some must be unlocked through a community-wide effort, while others are available to buy with Moon Flesh from the jump. And, of course, once the event ends, these will never return. Never ever.

I've been waking up at 6am everyday and doing missions for this Moon Flesh, and I've been doing it before bed as well. I, like many hopeless MMO/-live service players, am petrified that something in the game may never be mine to hoard. It has cut into my gym time, my morning coffee time, and indeed my sleep time. I owe my recent spree of unsubtle yawns in morning team meetings to Warframe. That's either a glowing endorsement, or a sign I need to ease up on this stuff. Who knows?

Am I allowed two entries? I'm not actually sure, but Bertie's not here to stop me so... ALSO , I have found myself consumed by Switch Sports Resort this week in a way I absolutely wasn't expecting to be when I fired it up for review . In my head, Nintendo's long-running series has always very much been a party game first, and an engaging solo endeavour a distant second.

But Switch Sports Resort is a bit of a treasure, and I've been having a great time with it on my own: taking it online for a bit of ranked or casual play, working through some achievements, or just firing up one of its fantastic open-world sightseeing modes for a leisurely explore. I hope Nintendo's got some post-launch plans in the works, because I'd love for it to go a little bit harder with the open-world stuff, particularly where flying is concerned. But until then there's skateboarding, which is bloody brilliant, and I'm already craving more.

items.title: "Devourer" Single Release
items.summary: The right tunes can make all the difference when travelling afar, and your upcoming journey to the Tau System is no exception. Fortunately, we've just made another stellar musical track from the ingenious Warframe Sound Team available for y
items.content:
The right tunes can make all the difference when travelling afar, and your upcoming journey to the Tau System is no exception. Fortunately, we've just made another stellar musical track from the ingenious Warframe Sound Team available for your listening pleasure on major streaming platforms. "Devourer," was first heard during the Epoch Operation: Taubound Official Gameplay Teaser. Influenced by slow, heavy metal from the likes of Black Sabbath, it features lyrics "sung" in Voidtongue, the terrifyingly enigmatic language of the Untime. This was a deliberate choice, recalling the memorable moment from 2023's Whispers in the Walls Quest when you took control of one of Albrecht Entrati's Vessels for the first time. Here, these elements combine for a musical experience that feels as massive and imposing as your latest endeavors ahead of Warframe: Tau, coming later this year.

items.title: ‘Warframe’ “Epoch Operation: Taubound” Event Live
items.summary: Late last week, Digital Extremes announced their latest event "Epoch Operation: Taubound" for their long-running sci-fi free-to-play looter shooter title
items.content:
Mobile News Nintendo PC PlayStation Xbox Genghis Husameddin

Late last week, Digital Extremes announced their latest event “Epoch Operation: Taubound” for their long-running sci-fi free-to-play looter shooter title ‘Warframe’—beckoning players to hop into the game’s monumental community event prior to the launch of “Tau”. New and returning players can tackle activities before Tuesday, 17 November, earning event rewards and collect resources to fuel the course to a new Star System, while diving back into The Lotus’ memories in a narrative Prologue Quest—Prologue to Tau.

The limited-time Epoch Operation: Taubound community event is comprised of two parts, a global objective to work towards, and a new narrative Prologue Quest:

Seek out greater challenges with the recently launched six-player mission type, The Icebind : Head to Yuvan Peak and recruit five other friends to form a squad of six, each with only one type of Warframe , for a new kind of game mode requiring heightened cooperation and teamwork. Offer up one Cryobell key per squadmate and vote on which set of randomized modifiers, like enemy faction, level layout, mission objectives, and potential debuffs, the team will need to overcome together. Coordinate strategies across four different phases and earn one of dozens of treasures to pick from Melica’s Glacial Laboratory upon completion.

“It’s no small task to travel the void of space toward an entirely new Star System, but I know the Warframe community is up for the challenge,” said Megan Everett , Community Director. “Community is our nexus. Our players are our champions. And so we call to them, new and returning, for this incredibly special time in Warframe’ s storied history, to rise to the occasion and reach for new stars. Together, we will discover what has become of Tau.”

Warframe is available across PC via Warframe.com /Steam (Windows & Linux via Proton), Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch consoles, iOS, and Android devices. Full cross-save and crossplay are supported across all platforms. And again, Warframe’s Tau update will be coming this way very soon.

Enjoying DayOne ? Do us a favour, and make us a ‘ Preferred Source on Google ‘ – that way, you’ll only be delivered more gaming coverage from our team.

There’s plenty of ways to become a part of DayOne. Head over and let us know your thoughts in the Day O ne Forums , the perfect place to chat about games if you’re a little more old-school and prefer things in a longform form, and if you mainly play on PC, join our Steam Community to connect with other members and maybe make some new friends!

Prefer the chaos of live and fast moving conversation? Come and make some noise in the lively DayOne Community Discord Server instead. If you’re rocking a DayOne Membership, both places give special access for our supporters, and you’ll unlock a ton of exclusive content, just for you.

items.title: How to play the Prologue to Tau quest in Warframe
items.content:
How to play the Prologue to Tau quest in Warframe One of the late-game warriors.

Anyone can jump into the new Taubound event, but the Prologue to Tau mission is harder to access. This one is for the vets, and you'll need to have put in the hours if you want to experience it for yourself. The good news is that, unlike the event itself, this quest will stick around, so even if you cannot play it now, you will be able to once you get far enough into the game.

To play this quest, you need to have completed The Old Peace and The Hex story quests, the two most recent quests in the game. If you have done that, and go visit your Codex on your ship, you will be able to access the new Prologue Quest and Chapters section, Prologue to Tau.

I don't want to get into spoiler territory, but it's definitely a first for Warframe to have you do what you do in this quest. Once you wrap up the quest, you will be awarded the Taubound Honoria. After that, you can crack on with Epoch Operation: Taubound and start paving the way to the next chapter of Warframe.

If you found this guide useful, b e sure to check out our Warframe page for more helpful guides.

items.title: Warframe Sets Course for a Distant Star System in Epoch Operation: Taubound
items.summary: In Epoch Operation: Taubound, new and returning XBOX players are invited to jump into missions on Eris in The Origin System, where they’ll destroy Infested enemies and obtain a new resource — Moonflesh.
items.content:
Community is the nexus of everything we do and every choice we make as Warframe developers. We create games with players, not just for players, and build trust over time through actions that demonstrate we listen. Our players around the world in our XBOX community are a monumental part of that family portrait; they help us make Warframe a better experience for everyone, and they deliver the critical feedback we need to ensure Warframe remains a safe, enjoyable space to spend a little time with friends and family online. To this day, I still pull out my XBOX 360 controller for our live TennoCon demos — it’s one of my favorite peripherals of all time.

Since Warframe debuted on XBOX One in 2014, we’ve thrived on stories and reports from our welcoming community of players across two generations of XBOX. In that time, we’ve brought them parity in content across platforms, introduced new ways to engage with a more global community with the introduction of cross-play and cross-save, and have dedicated platform-specific resources for players on XBOX to communicate with us directly.

From fan art, to handwritten thank-you letters, to bug reports and the constructive criticism we need to improve the experience day after day, and year after year, our XBOX community gives us the medicine we need to be stronger, smarter, and more inclusive. And we’re certainly not done yet.

From Warframe’s humble beginnings, we’ve teased the far-future narrative of Tau, a distant Star System shrouded in mystery. This year, we’re finally going together, and our community of XBOX players can help us get there. Alongside millions of players worldwide, we invite the community to join us in Epoch Operation: Taubound , arriving in Warframe on October 15. This unique, one-time community event will rally players everywhere, anywhere, for the ultimate cooperative challenge: fuel the trip to the distant Star System, Tau. Participation will be rewarded, and XBOX players won’t want to miss out before the event concludes on November 17.

In Epoch Operation: Taubound, new and returning XBOX players are invited to jump into missions on Eris in The Origin System, where they’ll destroy Infested enemies and obtain a new resource — Moonflesh — to power up the Sentient Mothership, Praghasa , and trade this curious new resource for event rewards. Coveted event rewards highlight what players on XBOX can discover and unlock alongside the community, including brand-new Armor Sets, exclusive event Honoria, Somachords, and other stunning cosmetics ranging from Glyphs, Sigils, Floofs, Syandanas, Signas, Badges, Blueprints, and so much more.

But that’s not all we have in store for our XBOX community. Also arriving is Prologue to Tau, a bite-sized entry in our single-player cinematic quest campaign that invites players to go hands-on with The Lotus for the first time ever (as seen during TennoLIVE 2026), setting the narrative stakes for this next monumental chapter in Warframe . Players can also finally use their Vessel they customized during TennoCon on the surface of Eris in a unique level and face off in a massive Infested boss fight. These permanent additions to Warframe ’s Quest Codex are not time-limited and are available to XBOX players who have completed The Hex and The Old Peace Quests.

From Tau and back, we are incredibly thankful to our XBOX community for being a part of this journey for 13+ years, and we look forward to the adventures ahead with you.

items.title: October in Warframe
items.summary: As the seasons change, so does the Origin System. And this October is no exception, with plenty of seasonal, returning, and brand new additions to occupy you as we draw ever closer to Warframe: Tau later this year. Watch for the following e
items.content:
As the seasons change, so does the Origin System. And this October is no exception, with plenty of seasonal, returning, and brand new additions to occupy you as we draw ever closer to Warframe: Tau later this year. Watch for the following events this month:

EPOCH OPERATION: TAUBOUND

October 15 - November 17 A unique event unlike anything you've experienced to date, Epoch Operation: Taubound offers all eligible Tenno the chance to become a part of Warframe history. If you want to help open up a path to the Tau System, be sure to have your account ready by completing the "Vor's Prize" Quest before October 15. Players looking to pilot their Vessel for the first time can also complete The Hex and The Old Peace in order to access a new, permanent Prologue Quest setting up the Road to Tau. For full event details – including prerequisites and more – click here.

NIGHTS OF NABERUS

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - November 2 @ 11 a.m. ET Spooky season returns to the Origin System during our annual Halloween-inspired event, with Daughter releasing her inventory of new and returning seasonal Customizations in exchange for Mother Tokens. While Baro Ki'Teer will mark the occasion in the same unsettling fashion as last year (IYKYK), we're also mixing it up by bringing back the Hallowed Nightmares Tactical Alert, allowing you to face off against the fearsome Jack O'Naut for even more Naberus treats. For all the harrowing details, check out our Halloween 2026 Events post.

NEW GAME MODE: THE ICEBIND

October 7 Originally intended to ship alongside Iceblade of Narin as "Glacial Defiance," our new 6-player game mode was ultimately delayed to allow for additional development time and renamed to The Icebind. Accessible in-game starting October 7, these challenging, high-level Missions can be played up to three times weekly, allowing you to put your teamwork (and Loadouts) to the test for valuable Rewards. Visit the official Warframe Forums to learn more about the delay, and further details of the game mode itself.

PRINCESS MARGARET CANCER FOUNDATION QUEST

October 1 - October 31 PMCF Quest (formerly Quest to Conquer Cancer) returns for another October full of special Community streams, donation incentives and Conquera Customizations. Join us all month long and help support The Princess Margaret Cancer Foundation light the way towards a world free from the fear of cancer. Visit the Warframe PMCF Quest webpage for more information or donate directly here.

Protea Prime

A master of battlefield preparation, Protea Prime brings tactical ingenuity and devastating technology to every mission. Deploy her arsenal, control the flow of combat and keep your squad supplied while turning the battlefield to your advantage. Protea Prime is a versatile addition to any Arsenal, giving Tenno the tools to adapt to whatever the Origin System throws their way.

Ivara Prime

Stalking from the shadows and waiting for the perfect moment to strike, Ivara Prime is a huntress ready to claim her prey. Ivara Prime draws her bow and disappears into the shadows before striking with deadly precision. With a versatile Quiver, powerful Artemis Bow and the ability to move unseen, Ivara Prime is a natural choice for Tenno who prefer stealth and careful execution.

Prime Warframes

Want to learn more about Prime Warframes? Check out our Guide to Prime Warframes video for a helpful breakdown of what Prime Warframes are, different ways you can earn them and how you can purchase Prime items.

items.title: Iceblade of Narin Official Soundtrack
items.summary: Amid the frigid fanfare of our Iceblade of Narin launch, we're proud to once again deliver Warframe's latest musical tracks to major streaming platforms for your listening enjoyment. The talent, creativity and ingenuity of our remarkable So
items.content:
Amid the frigid fanfare of our Iceblade of Narin launch, we're proud to once again deliver Warframe's latest musical tracks to major streaming platforms for your listening enjoyment. The talent, creativity and ingenuity of our remarkable Sound Team reverberates across the three tracks comprising this release. Drawing inspiration from a traditional Korean musical style called Sanjo, each song evokes the powerful, dynamic movements of a sword dancer — just like our 66th Warframe, Narin. The melodies recorded for Neote's Dance also inspired the vocals in Ice Speaker, which further combines familiar tunes associated with both the Zariman and the Man in the Wall for a unique aural motif befitting the narrative strands threaded through our latest update (as well as the intensity of the upcoming Glacial Defiance game mode).

Where can I listen?

You can find the Iceblade of Narin Official Soundtrack on:
  • Spotify
  • Apple Music
  • YouTube Music
  • Amazon Music
  • Tidal

  • Janggu: John Lee

2. Ice Speaker

  • Composer: Matthew Chalmers
  • Producers: Erich Preston, Matthew Chalmers
  • Vocals: CECILIA

items.content:
The overwhelming talent of our community artists is on full display with TennoGen Iceblade, now available on all platforms! This all-new collection brings several absolutely ravishing Customizations that will surely add some opulent flair to your Fashion Frame. This brand-new release includes:
  • Vermis Signa by Travelling Merchant and Therion
  • Gothica Signa by malaya, Jadie and Awk’Q-Luz
  • Jade Coven Skin by blazingcobalt
  • Citrine Heliotropia Skin by Ventralhound
  • Reliquia Syandana by lex182 and Therion

TennoGen Iceblade Bundles

Please note: For those Tenno on Console and Mobile, these items are available via two Bundles on the in-game Market:

TennoGen Iceblade Bundle 1

  • Reliquia Syandana
  • Vermis Signa
  • Gothica Signa

TennoGen Iceblade Bundle 2

  • Jade Coven Skin
  • Citrine Heliotropia Skin
We can’t thank our amazing TennoGen Artists enough for these wonderful contributions and we are so proud to have their work be part of our Iceblade of Narin update!
